discovery: Plasma wakefield acceleration of particles by laser- and beam-driven plasma waves

nominees.name: Chandrashekhar Joshi
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

subfield: Plasma physics / laser-plasma interaction and accelerator physics
motivation: Tajima's 1979 proposal (with the late J. M. Dawson) showed that an intense laser pulse can drive a plasma wave whose electric fields exceed those of conventional accelerators by three orders of magnitude. Joshi's experiments turned this into reality. He demonstrated beat-wave and later beam-driven plasma wakefield acceleration, including energy doubling of 42 GeV electrons in under a metre of plasma at SLAC. Malka's group produced quasi-monoenergetic, controllably injected laser-wakefield electron beams and pioneered their use as compact sources of radiation. Together they established plasma-based acceleration as a quantitative, predictive science. Its kinetic nonlinear wave-particle physics is now matched by experiment. It promises table-top accelerators and X-ray sources for medicine, materials science and future colliders. This is a field-founding achievement that connects elegant plasma theory with transformative technology.
